issues.detail: The Hebrew 'וַיִּשְׁלַח ... עֲלֵיהֶם בְּיַד מַלְאָכָיו' means 'He sent [word] to them by His messengers' (i.e., He sent prophets/messengers to them), but the Chinese '藉著自己的天使屢次伸手差遣他們' renders '祂藉著自己的天使差遣他們' — making the messengers the agents who are sent, and '他們' (them) the object of sending, which reverses the direction: in Hebrew, the messengers are the means by which YHWH sends to the people (the people are the recipients, not the ones sent). This changes who is doing what to whom.

The Hebrew 'הַשְׁכֵּם וְשָׁלוֹחַ' (literally 'rising early and sending') is an emphatic idiom meaning 'sending persistently/again and again'. The Chinese '屢次伸手差遣' captures the repetition but adds '伸手' (stretch out hand) which is not in the Hebrew, and the phrase 'עֲלֵיהֶם' ('upon/against them') is not explicitly rendered; the Chinese says '差遣他們' (send them) rather than 'send to them'.
